title: What Am I Missing?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This short Admired Leadership Field Note argues that "What am I missing?" is one of the most powerful expressions in a leader's repertoire, alongside "I don't know," "I'm counting on you" and "Tell me more." The phrase works because it assumes the leader's view is incomplete and invites others to fill the gap, whereas "Any questions?" and "Does everyone agree?" invite people to confirm what the leader already believes. The piece warns that the question only works if the leader means it, because team members watch what happens after someone offers a missing piece. The best leaders treat every answer as a gift, thank the person, ask a follow-up and say out loud when the input has changed their mind. Over time the habit compounds: leaders hear about problems while there is still time to fix them, and people learn that their judgment, not just their agreement, is wanted.
points: The wording matters: "What am I missing?" presupposes an incomplete view, which turns dissent from a risk into a contribution, unlike confirmation-seeking questions such as "Does everyone agree?"
The question is only as credible as the leader's reaction, because defending the original view after someone offers a gap teaches the team the question was a formality.
Strong leaders respond with thanks and a follow-up question, and name the moment when someone's input changed their thinking.
A visible change of mind encourages others to speak up next time, so the habit compounds into earlier warning of problems.
The expression models a confidence that does not depend on being right, which is what makes people willing to bring bad news.
